recentItems.title: Ex-WSJ reporter comments on union suppression in Hong Kong after court convicts publisher
recentItems.description:
(10 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Hong Kong - 10 September 2026

1. Wide of former Wall Street Journal reporter and chairperson of the trade union, Hong Kong Journalists Association Selina Cheng walking out of the court building entrance with her team of lawyers
2. Various of photojournalists taking pictures of Selina Cheng outside Eastern Law Courts Building entrance
3. SOUNDBITE (English), Selina Cheng, former Wall Street Journal reporter and Chairperson of The Hong Kong Journalists Association:
“The private persecutions, I believe has brought a lot of awareness into the idea of union suppression in Hong Kong and I hope that employers will see that they have no right to have the employees consult with them before the employees join the union. And I hope that employees will see from this case that they also shouldn’t seek, consult with their employers on that. Otherwise, it would be just handing the right over to the employers.”
4. Mid of Hong Kong Eastern Law Courts Building entrance
5. SOUNDBITE (English), Selina Cheng, former Wall Street Journal reporter and Chairperson of The Hong Kong Journalists Association:
"If reporters' employment rights are not sufficiently safeguarded or when their rights are violated and not enforced in law, then we can no longer work safely as reporters."
6. Mid of Selina Cheng hugging one of the lawyers representing her after verdict 
7. Mid of Selina Cheng leaving court
8. Various of Hong Kong Eastern Law Courts Building entrance
STORYLINE:
Hong Kong Eastern Law Courts on Thursday found the publisher of The Wall Street Journal(WSJ) guilty of trying to prevent one of its reporters from taking a leadership role in a local press union, but acquitted the company of a charge that it fired her because of her union activities. 

Talking to reporters outside the court, Cheng said that the case has brought awareness of union suppression in Hong Kong and that she hoped employers will understand they have no right to have their employees consult with them before their workers join a union. 

"If reporters' employment rights are not sufficiently safeguarded or when their rights are violated and not enforced in law, then we can no longer work safely as reporters," Selina Cheng said.

Former WSJ reporter Selina Cheng launched a private prosecution against Dow Jones Publishing Co. (Asia) Inc. after losing her job in July 2024. 

The case has raised concerns about media freedom in the Chinese territory. Cheng and the journalists’ association are advocates of press freedom but have been operating under pressure since the government cracked down on pro-democracy media and political dissent. The government has been critical of the union.

Cheng earlier said that her supervisor told her that her participation in the union election was problematic and that the supervisor needed to discuss the issue with WSJ's management in New York and Dow Jones’ in-house lawyers. Cheng said that she was told that her union role would be incompatible with her employment.

Dow Jones said that it respectfully disagrees with the ruling and is evaluating its next step. It said the Journal has a “long and proud history” as an employer in Hong Kong.

AP video shot by Alice Fung

recentItems.title: Sumac production thriving in Iraq's semi-autonomous northern Kurdish region
recentItems.description:
(10 Sep 2026) 
IRAQ SUMAC

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

LENGTH: 3:55

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Dohuk, Iraq – 30 August 2026
1. Various drone shots of sumac farms in mountains around Dohuk
2. Close of sumac buds on trees
3. Various of farmer harvesting sumac buds 
4. SOUNDBITE (Kurdish) Nimat Abu Zeid, farmer from Harn village in Dohuk:
“Well, this is the only way to harvest, there are no other ways. We pick it by hand, clean it, move it and put it on this (plastic) sheet. Then, we crush it and transfer it by car that we have here.”

5. Various of Nimat carrying a bag full of sumac in the fields
6. Nimat emptying the bag on plastic sheet
7. Various of woman beating and crushing sumac branches
8. Farmers working on refining sumac buds
9. SOUNDBITE (Kurdish) Magri Mustafa, worker in sumac harvesting and refining:
“It is a nice (spice) and can be used on anything. It can be added to food and gives it a sour flavour. Also, it can be added to salad, and cucumber. I mean to everything. It adds flavour to everything. It adds a unique sour flavour to food, and it is much better than adding citric acid or other things.”

10. Various of workers harvesting sumac in farm
11. Close on bag
12. Various of workers filling in sack with sumac buds
13. Workers loading sumac sacks into truck 
14. SOUNDBITE (Kurdish) Nimat Abu Zeid, farmer from Harn village in Dohuk:
“We are taking it to Dinarta (township) as there are sumac traders there. We are selling it to them, and I don’t know if they are reselling it to markets abroad. We don’t know that. The prices are good this year. Now, the red type is worth up to 10,000 dinar ($3.2 per pound) while the white type and according to what I heard; worth up to 12,000 to 13,000 dinar ($4.0-$8.2 per pound)."

15. Man unloading sumac sacks by shop in town
16. Various of shop worker checking quality of sumac
17. Sumac trader talking to farmers 
18. Crushed and refined sumac bags on shelves inside shop 
19. SOUNDBITE (Kurdish) Masoud Mohammed, sumac trader in Dinarta:
“We sell most of the sumac we have inside Kurdistan, the cities in Kurdistan (semi-autonomous region in Iraq) along with cities in Iraq. We are sending it to southern Iraq, but we haven’t sent it abroad (that much). Actually, we sent a small amount to various cities abroad. However, since the prices are high, it is unprofitable to send it abroad. We won’t make any profits.”

20. Wide of landscape around sumac farms 
21. Directorate of Agriculture Department building in Dinarta 
22. SOUNDBITE (Kurdish) Mahdi Taha, director of agriculture department in Dinarta:
“We are expecting that the sumac production this year will be 6000 tons, as we have 9000 dunums (2223 acres) of land being planted with sumac. There is an increase in sumac production and that’s due to the suitable weather of our area, which is very appropriate for sumac production.”

23. Drone shot of sumac farms in Harn village in Dinarta 
STORYLINE:
A dark red spice, tangy and rich, has been providing a livelihood for Kurdish villagers near Dohuk in the semi-autonomous region of northern Iraq. 

It's called sumac, derived from the Arabic word, and it's a staple in Middle Eastern cooking, sprinkled on anything from Hummus to the ubiquitous Arab salad fattoush, and grilled meats. 

"It adds flavour to everything. It adds a unique sour flavour to food, and it is much better than adding citric acid or other things," said worker Magri Mustafa. 


Starting in July and continuing until September, farmers harvest sumac buds by hand and transfer them to a plastic sheet.






AP video by Rashid Yahya

recentItems.title: Mourners gather as Israeli strike on Gaza home kills family of four, including two young girls
recentItems.description:
(10 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

++CLIENTS PLEASE NOTE: EDIT CONTAINS FOOTAGE OF BODY BAGS OF CHILDREN++

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 10 September 2026
1. Various of people carrying body bags of four members from one family, parents and their daughters who were killed in an Israeli airstrike, out of the morgue and placing on the ground 
2. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Zuheir Al-Heisami, resident of Beit Lahiya:
"Day and night, the shooting never stops. Shells and shrapnel rain down on us and on the tents. People are being wounded and killed by the gunfire and shelling."
3. Various of body bags of the two young girls on the ground, reading (Arabic) "The child Dana Ahmed, the child Bana Ahmed, 10/9/2026"
4. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Zuheir Al-Heisami, resident of Beit Lahiya:
"There is no justification for Israel to strike this house. Two young girls, along with their mother and father, were asleep—it was 02:00 am when the four-story building was bombed while the children were asleep"
5. Various of people carrying body bags and placing them in an ambulance 
6. Mid of ambulance leaving 
STORYLINE:
An Israeli strike on Thursday at a family house in northern Gaza killed a family of four.

The strike on Beit Lahia killed a husband and wife, alongside their two daughters, 8 and 12.

The bodies were taken to Shifa Hospital in Gaza City before they were sent to burial.

“There is no justification for Israel to strike this house,” said Zuheir al-Heisami, a neighbor of the family, at the hospital. 

He said the strike happened at around 2 am and added that "these were two children and their parents that were killed while they were asleep.”

There was no immediate comment from the Israeli military on the strike early Thursday, but a new statement said its forces on Wednesday struck Hamas weapons storage facilities in three areas across Gaza. 

Israel’s military in the past has said it carries out strikes in response to threats against its forces under the fragile ceasefire that has been in place since October.

AP Production by Wafaa Shurafa

recentItems.title: French tanker refuels US F-22 Raptors in rare operation over Alaska
recentItems.description:
(10 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
In Air on Alaska - 9 September 2026 
1. Wide of French aircraft Multi-Role Tanker Transport (MRTT) tanker pilots navigating an aircraft over Alaska
2. Wide of Alaskan mountain range seen from an aircraft
3. Various of snow-covered mountains in Alaska
4. Wide of F-22 Raptor jet flying over Alaska as part of a military exercise
5. Mid of a pilot monitoring F-22 flight operations on control screens in Alaska
6. Close of an F-22 Raptor being refueled mid-air over Alaska
7. Wide of French air force Rafale fighter jet 
8. Close of the refueling hose for French air force Rafale fighter
9. Mid of French Air Force Rafale fighter jet refueling 
10. SOUNDBITE (French) Officer Adrien, the French air refueling operator:
“Today we refueled F-22s. It’s only the second time we’ve done that with French MRTTs. It’s a very large aircraft for a fighter, so when we saw it approaching from a distance, we thought, ‘Wow, it’s pretty big.’ The main difficulty was the stress because I had never done it before. Even on the simulator, we don’t really have the F-22 in our parameters. But the conditions were very favorable, the aircraft was extremely stable, and we managed to make contact perfectly, without any damage.”
11. Mid of F-22 Raptor jet flying over Alaska skies
12. Wide of French Air Force Rafale fighter jet refueling with F22 
13. Mid of F-22 fighter jet flying over Alaska
14. French Air Force Rafale fighter jet refueling mid-air over Alaska
15. Close up of a pilot's hand gripping the control stick inside an F-22 cockpit in Alaska
16. SOUNDBITE (French) Officer Adrien, the French air refueling operator:
 “You have to aim carefully and position the boom properly to avoid making contact with the aircraft itself. The goal is to make a very precise contact and go directly into the receptacle without touching the edges, the doors, or even the paint, which is a special coating on an aircraft like the F-22 because of its stealth characteristics.”
17. French air force Rafale fighter jet  mid-air over Alaska
18. Close of French Air Force Rafale fighter jet refueling mid-air over Alaska

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Eielson Air Force Base, Alaska - 9 September 2026
19. Capt. Julien, French Rafale pilot, walking in corridor
20. SOUNDBITE (English) Capt. Julien, French Rafale pilot:
"We had the opportunity to fly against F-22 Raptor, which is one of the best aircraft for air defense in the world. We initially performed a mixed join-up on a French refueling aircraft that initially refueled both F-22 Raptors with a boom configuration which is not the same as a problem drogue for rifle fighters. So, in a really efficient time, the French tanker did the refueling of the Raptor, and then quickly changed the configuration to set into problem drogue configuration to give us for Rafale part the fuel necessary for the combat mission"

ASSOCIATED PRESS
In Air on Alaska- 9 Septemeber 2026 
21. French air force Rafale fighter jet mid-air over Alaska
22. Wide of F-22 fighter jets flying in formation over Alaska
23. Mid of F-22 Raptor flying over Alaska, showcasing advanced military capabilities

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Eielson Air Force Base, Alaska - 9 September 2026
24. SOUNDBITE (English) Capt. Julien, French Rafale pilot:
"We split the flight into two mixed patrols, one with a raffle F-22 and the other one also with a Raffle F22 to perform some visual range combat maneuver and fight each other for about 30 minutes."
25. Mid of French Air & Space Force jacket patch 
26. SOUNDBITE (English) Capt. Julien, French Rafale pilot:

recentItems.title: A new Ebola treatment center opens in Kisangani as Congo’s outbreak spreads
recentItems.description:
(10 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kisangani, DR Congo – 9 September 2026

1. Ebola riposte team visiting the new Ebola Treatment Center (ETC)
2. Mid of Ebola Treatment Center installations
3. Mid of consultation room of the Ebola Treatment Center
4. Doctors Without Borders (MSF) staff explaining about the ETC
5. SOUNDBITE (French) Kate Nolan, MSF emergency coordinator based in Kisangani:  
“Having an Ebola Treatment Center (ETC) with all the necessary support services, sufficient treatment capacity, and good access to patients will, of course, improve the ability of the medical staff to provide the best possible care to patients and also provide access to an isolation facility to break the chain of transmission at the community level.”
6. Various of Ebola riposte team visiting the Ebola treatment center
7. Mid of Dr. Simon Bokongo, Provincial Minister of Health for Tshopo washing hands outside the center
8. SOUNDBITE (French) Dr. Simon Bokongo, Provincial Minister of Health for Tshopo: 
“This is the 17th (Ebola) outbreak; people have died, and people have been affected. So, we need to be aware that the disease is here.”
9. Wide of workers in the Ebola Treatment center
10. Wide of healthcare workers at washing kit
11. Mid of officials visiting ETC
12. SOUNDBITE (French) Dr. Bienvenu Ikomo Bitalo, Head of the Ebola Response in Kisangani:  
“First and foremost, you must avoid all physical contact, because Ebola (cannot be treated) with nebulizer as we saw with COVID. I also see people wearing masks today. No! That’s not how it works with Ebola. With Ebola, it’s all about avoiding contact.””
13. Mid of Ebola riposte team in the ETC
STORYLINE:
The Ebola response team, with Doctors Without Borders and Congolese authorities, inaugurated a new Ebola treatment center in the city of Kisangani, in Tshopo Province, as authorities battle the outbreak, which has claimed nearly 3,200 lives among more than 6,600 confirmed cases.

ETC is equipped with 22 beds but with an operational capacity of 50 beds.

Kate Nolan, MSF emergency coordinator based in Kisangani highlighted that the ETC will "improve the ability of the medical staff to provide the best possible care to patients” to "break the chain of transmission at the community level”.

The Kisangani Ebola Treatment Center will incorporate strict infection prevention and control standards, including handwashing stations, separate pathways for suspected and confirmed cases, waste management systems, cleaning and disinfection procedures, and staff training on the use of personal protective equipment.

The Ebola outbreak is spreading across six provinces in eastern Congo in some of the most difficult conditions imaginable, fueled by rebel violence, displacement and intense population movements. 

A weak healthcare and surveillance system also challenges responders, and insufficient contact tracing and laboratory testing.

Efforts to contain the outbreak have also been complicated by the lack of an approved vaccine or treatment for the rare Bundibugyo virus causing it. 

Authorities have started vaccinating front-line health workers with the Ervebo vaccine, which the World Health Organization says could offer some protection against Ebola but there’s no conclusive evidence that it would work against the current virus.

recentItems.title: China MOFA Highlights - 10 September 2026
recentItems.description:
(10 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS -  
Beijing, China -  10 September 2026

Spokesperson: Guo Jiakun

1.India’s Serious Fraud Office has recommended that China’s Xiaomi be investigated for alleged irregularities in its business model and compliance with foreign investment law. What is China’s comment on this?

I am not familiar with the specifics you mentioned. Economic and trade cooperation between China and India is, in nature, mutually beneficial and win-win. We hope India will provide a fair, just, transparent, and non-discriminatory business environment for companies from all countries investing and operating in India.

2.During his meeting with Ambassador David Perdue to China, Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged both sides to work to eliminate interference and overcome obstacles ahead of the expected summit between President Xi and President Trump. Are there any examples of obstacles that China believes are within the US ability to tackle, or in general, are both sides making any progress in recent communications in dealing with these obstacles? 

We have issued relevant information on Foreign Minister Wang Yi's meeting with US Ambassador David Perdue. Leaders' diplomacy plays an irreplaceable strategic guiding role in China-US relations. The two sides keep in touch regarding the arrangement of leaders' interactions within the year. 

3.According to media reports, the U.S. Embassy in Panama recently held an internal briefing to introduce a pilot project to build the world’s first certification and traceability platform for artificial intelligence supply chains in Panama, and revealed that the project has entered the evaluation stage. Commentators said that the project could be part of the U.S. efforts to control technology supply chains and contain China’s technological development. What is China’s comment?

We noted the reports. Artificial intelligence concerns the well-being of all humanity, and all parties should adhere to the principles of openness and inclusiveness and ensure that it promotes the well-being of humanity as a force for good and for all. Forming closed and exclusive small groupings and engaging in geopolitical calculations are not conducive to technological development and progress in the Global South, including Latin American and Caribbean countries.
China is ready to work with all parties including Latin American and Caribbean countries to jointly build a fair and reasonable global governance system for artificial intelligence and to ensure that it benefits people in all countries.

4.Does China have any comments on the U.S. federal trial against Huawei that began on Wednesday in New York? A US prosecutor called Huawei a criminal enterprise stealing from American companies. 

The Chinese government firmly opposes the US suppressing and containing Chinese companies and resolutely supports its companies in safeguarding their legitimate rights and interests.  

5.Nepal is planning to ask wealthier countries and agencies for financial help this week. Has Nepal asked China for financial help and does China plan to contribute?

Following this disaster, while urgently carrying out rescue efforts at home, China immediately extended a helping hand to Nepal to support its emergency relief efforts. As a traditional friendly neighbor, China is willing to provide assistance within its capabilities for Nepal’s post-disaster reconstruction in accordance with Nepal’s needs. We believe that under the leadership of the Nepalese government, the people of Nepal will surely overcome the disaster and rebuild their homes as soon as possible.

recentItems.title: Discover the restored underground ancient Roman fresco and mosaic
recentItems.description:
(10 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Rome, Italy - 8 September 2026
1. Close of face on mosaic
2. Close of newly discovered sections at bottom of mosaic showing port city
3. SOUNDBITE: (Italian) Roberto Gualtieri, Mayor of Rome: ++SOUNDBITE OVERLAID BY SHOT 4++
“They had not only traditional thermal facilities, but also, for the first time, gardens, places for sports and places of culture. In fact, most likely, archaeologists understood that the exedra above us contained the shelves of a library.”
4. Various close of mosaic and columns
5. Top shot of newly restored five-metre-high mosaic
6. SOUNDBITE: (Italian) Roberto Gualtieri, Mayor of Rome: ++SOUNDBITE OVERLAID BY SHOT 7, SHOT 8 AND SHOT 9+
“Above all, it allows you to see, to have a view of a Roman city as it was and of a Roman port. The lower part of the port was discovered by our archaeologists recently. In short, it is a detailed description of a port of extraordinary wealth, very dense with buildings and colonnades. It is impressive to see that Roman ports were like this. They’re not so strong now, so it’s really something unique.”
7. Close of newly discovered sections at bottom of mosaic showing port city
8. Ceiling to floor of mosaic
8. Close of faun between columns on mosaic
9. Corner of room with wall covered by mosaic
10. Various close of mosaic
STORYLINE:
From high up you get glimpses of this important underground discovery. 

This is the recently restored “Painted City” fresco and “Great Mosaic” which were found in an underground gallery during excavations in the 1990s of the Baths of Trajan on the Oppio hill near the Colosseum.

Now the works are being opened to the public for the first time, initially to small groups of 15, and during a trial period of weekend access starting this month. 

The aim is to determine how the delicate works respond to increased humidity and climactic impacts before allowing more general access.

Rome's Mayor Roberto Gualtieri explains the importance of the  Baths of Trajan : “They had not only traditional thermal facilities, but also, for the first time, gardens, places for sports and places of culture. In fact, most likely, archaeologists understood that the exedra above us contained the shelves of a library.”

The mosaic is some 15 meters high and features intricately decorated columns and architectural elements and figures over four different levels. 

The top levels seem like a theatrical scene, while at the bottom are designs of another depiction of a port city that were only recently discovered during the restoration.

“It is a subject that develops across four levels because we have the two upper levels with this perspective of a scene that is almost theatrical, that is organised with stands and architectural projections that are truly surprising”  says Claudio Parisi Presicce, Rome’s cultural superintendent.

The Baths of Trajan, which were dedicated by Emperor Trajan in 109 AD, extended over six hectares and were at the time the largest bath complex in the world. 

They incorporated an earlier bath complex, the Domus Aurea, and was designed on a different trajectory to take better advantage of the water temperatures to optimize the thermal experience for users.

The complex now open to the public includes a grand semicircular upper-level “library” which archaeologists believe was part of the bath complex and allowed users not only to practice sport and bathe, but also to participate in cultural activities.




AP Video by Lorenzo Gironacci
